content:
The Time, Speed & Distance chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Time, Speed & Distance tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Time, Speed & Distance

Speed–distance–time, relative speed, trains, boats and streams, races and average speed.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Speed = Distance/Time; x km/h = x·5/18 m/s.
  • Two equal distances at u and v: average = 2uv/(u+v) (harmonic mean).
  • Relative speed = u−v (same direction), u+v (opposite).
  • Boat: downstream b+s, upstream b−s.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Taking the simple mean of two speeds for equal distances (use the harmonic mean).
  • Forgetting to add the train’s own length when crossing a platform.
  • Sign errors in relative speed.

faq.q: What is the average speed for equal distances?
faq.a: The harmonic mean 2uv/(u+v), NOT the arithmetic mean.

faq.q: How long to cross a platform?
faq.a: Time = (train length + platform length)/speed; for a pole it is just train length/speed.
